blocks.text: Softmax turns a list of numbers (scores) into positive weights that add up to 1. Larger scores get larger weights.

The exponential of a large score overflows. $e^{1000}$ is infinity in floating point. The fix is to subtract the largest score first. This does not change the result, because the same factor $e^{-\max}$ appears in the numerator and the denominator.
With scores (1000, 999, 998) the naive formula returns `nan` for every weight. The shifted formula returns (0.6652, 0.2447, 0.09003). Question [[q:223|223]] asks for this stable version.

If every score is $-\infty$ (all positions masked), the shifted formula divides $-\infty$ by $-\infty$ and returns `nan`. Question 328 handles this case by returning zeros. See [[article:attention-masks|Attention masks]].
